WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:51390  CRL.P No. 12517 of 2024  ORAL ORDER Accused in Spl.C.(POCSO)No.5/2024 pending before the Court of II Additional District and Sessions Judge FTSC, Chitradurga, arising out of Crime No.191/2023 registered by Imangala Police Station, Chitradurga for offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376 of IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking regular bail.
2. Heard the learned counsel for parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.191/2023 was registered by Imangala Police Station initially for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC against unknown persons on the basis of the first information dated 19.11.2023 received from the respondent No.2, who is the mother of the victim girl.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge FTSC, Chitradurga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: During the course of investigation, petitioner and the victim girl were traced.
The petitioner was arrested on 21.11.2023 and subsequently, remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation of the case was completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Bail application filed by the petitioner before the Trial Court was rejected on 19.06.2024.

Therefore, he had approached this NC: 2024:KHC:51390 Court in Crl.P.7552/2024 which was dismissed as not pressed on 22.08.2024 with liberty to the petitioner to file a fresh petition, after the cross-examination of the victim girl (PW.1) is completed before the Trial Court.
Therefore, petitioner is before this Court in this successive bail petition.
4. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that the victim girl has been completely examined before the Trial Court as PW.1.
Petitioner aged about 22 years having no criminal antecedents is in custody.
Chances of Trial being completed in the near future is very remote.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the petition.
6. Learned High Court Government Pleader submits that victim is a minor and she has supported the case of the prosecution during the course of investigation.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: First information was submitted by the mother of the victim girl on 19.11.2023 and in the first information it is averred that the minor daughter of the first informant was NC: 2024:KHC:51390 found missing from her house on 18.11.2023.
Efforts made to trace her had failed.
Therefore, first informant had approached police.
During the course of investigation of the case, petitioner and the victim girl were traced.
Petitioner was arrested and remanded to judicial custody on 21.11.2023.
The victim girl has been now examined before the Trial Court as PW.1.
Victim girl has stated that she was acquainted with the petitioner and they were chatting regularly on Instagram.
She has also stated that she was in love with the petitioner.
Petitioner aged about 22 years who has no other criminal antecedents is in custody for the last more than 1 year.
Since the victim girl has been completely examined before the Trial Court, there cannot be any apprehension that the petitioner is likely to tamper with the material charge sheet witnesses.
Prosecution in all has cited 27 charge sheet witnesses in the present case and till date only one witness has been examined.

Therefore,
chances of the trial being completed and case being disposed of on its merits in the near soon is very remote.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail requires to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:51390 ORDER The petition is allowed.
